teaser.text: BAE Systems sells the machinery, electronics, software and long-term service that governments use to defend themselves. Its business is best understood as a long chain: public money enters through programmes, flows to people and suppliers, and returns as profit only after BAE has delivered what it promised.

stock.title: BAE Systems stock forecast
stock.meta_description: BAE Systems stock forecast: weighted scenarios through October 2029, plus the backlog, margins, cash flow and valuation shaping each case.
stock.opening: BAE Systems' weighted forecast reaches 1867.04 GBp in October 2029; the bear, base and bull cases carry 30%, 50% and 20% probabilities. It hinges on BAE Systems converting its backlog into delivered output, retained margins and ordinary cash.
stock.closing: The full BAE Systems memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could BAE Systems' shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast keeps BAE Systems close to today’s price, with modest positive total return only by October 2029. The weighted prices are 1806.07 GBp in October 2027, with a negative 2% return including dividends, and 1826.09 GBp in October 2028, with a 1% return. By October 2029, the weighted price reaches 1867.04 GBp, a 6% total return.

The range is much wider than the weighted outcome: by October 2029, the bear case is 1083.54 GBp and the bull case is 3313.14 GBp, against today’s 1882.50 GBp. The probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for BAE Systems, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base earnings row is £2,534m in October 2027. It rises to £2,726m in October 2028 and reaches £2,926m in October 2029. The base margin path moves from 7.8% to 8.1%, reflecting delivery of most of management’s upgraded plan without assuming a dramatic recovery in Maritime. The bear row gives £2,247m at the first date and £2,271m at the second, because advances unwind and fixed-price ship work absorbs costs. It reaches £2,342m at the last date. The bull starts at £2,738m and reaches £3,068m in the second year, then £3,393m, because capacity, suppliers and accepted deliveries convert demand into operating leverage. Maritime return on sales had fallen to 6.1%, which argues against making the bull case the central case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does BAE Systems really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the cash left after the deductions chosen by the company or analyst. BAE’s own measure includes joint-venture dividends and deducts selected capital, lease and interest items. A stricter measure deducts gross capital spending, lease payments and interest paid. Stock-based pay creates another adjustment: it is not a cash payment at grant, but it compensates employees and therefore belongs in an economic cash assessment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for BAE Systems?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from £19,521m in 2021 to £28,336m in 2025, while operating margin fell from 12.2% to 10.3%. Computed free cash flow—cash from operations minus capital spending—peaked at an 8.9% margin in 2023 and fell to 5.1% in 2025. Net debt fell from £5,034m in 2024 to £3,847m in 2025. Computed free cash flow per share fell from 66.57p in 2023 to 48.04p in 2025. At 1,882.50p, the shares trade at 27.0x trailing earnings and 19.6x next-12-month earnings, with a 2.9% free-cash-flow yield and 1.9% dividend yield.

dividend.title: BAE Systems dividend: cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: BAE Systems' dividend, cash coverage, future scenarios and yield, explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: BAE Systems' dividend is forecast to rise from £0.399 to £0.483 per share, with the base case extending the recent 10% annual growth pattern. Across 2021–2025, BAE Systems generated £8,826m of free cash flow and paid £7,174m through dividends and buybacks; in 2025, only £15m remained after those distributions.
dividend.closing: The full BAE Systems memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does BAE Systems pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base case from £0.399 to £0.439 and then £0.483 per share. That extends the recent 10% annual growth pattern and fits the policy of sustainable cover around two times underlying earnings. The bear path moves from £0.37 to £0.35 and then holds, as cash conversion weakens. The bull reaches £0.42, £0.49 and £0.57 as earnings and cash generation accelerate.

blocks.heading: Does BAE Systems' cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Across 2021–2025, BAE generated £8,826m of free cash flow and paid £7,174m through dividends and buybacks. In 2025, only £15m remained after those distributions. Free cash flow therefore did not mean cash available for any acquisition: shareholders had already received most of it.

blocks.heading: What could change BAE Systems' dividend?

paragraphs.text: The bear case would gain weight during 2027–2028 if customer advances unwind while completed work fails to produce ordinary receipts, weakening free cash flow and raising net debt. It would strengthen through 2027–2029 if fixed-price cost revisions push Maritime and group margins lower.

blocks.heading: What is BAE Systems' dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The 1.9% dividend yield is therefore a supporting measure, not the main investment case. Earnings must survive programme execution, and cash must survive the spending that follows advances.
